1.mascotDialogue: An arrow in a directed graph means exactly one thing — you may travel this way. It says nothing at all about whether you may return.

2.mascotDialogue: Line 8 sets exactly one cell in the matrix. A directed edge only ever writes adjacency[u][v] — never adjacency[v][u].

3.mascotDialogue: Every arrowhead points only one way here. This particular loop happens to form a cycle, yes, but each edge remains, individually, one-directional.

4.mascotDialogue: This is the single most common mistake with directed graphs — treating a one-way arrow as though it secretly runs both ways. It does not. The visual only ever draws the direction you actually assigned.
